title: Building a Small Project: Putting It All Together
summary: In this final lesson you will combine the concepts learned to create a simple, functional program. You will also learn how to plan, code, test, and improve a small project.

sections.heading: Project Planning
sections.body:
Before writing any code, decide what your program will do. A good beginner project is a "Guess the Number" game where the computer picks a random number and the user tries to guess it.

Write down the main steps: generate a random number, ask the user for a guess, compare the guess to the target, give feedback, and repeat until the correct number is guessed.

sections.heading: Implementing the Core Logic
sections.body:
Start a new file in your IDE and import the random module. Create a variable for the secret number using random.randint(1, 100). Then write a while loop that continues until the user guesses correctly.

Inside the loop, use input() to read the user's guess, convert it to an integer, and use if‑else statements to tell the user if the guess is too low, too high, or correct.

sections.heading: Adding Features and Error Handling
sections.body:
Enhance the game by counting how many attempts the user makes and displaying the total at the end. Wrap the input conversion in a try‑except block to handle non‑numeric entries gracefully.

When an error occurs, inform the user and ask for another guess without crashing the program.

sections.heading: Testing and Debugging
sections.body:
Run the program several times to check all paths: correct guess on first try, too low, too high, and invalid input. Use print statements or a debugger to verify that the attempt counter updates correctly.

If a bug appears, read the error message, locate the line, and fix the logic. Remember to test edge cases like guessing 1 or 100.

quiz.q: Which Python statement is used to repeat actions until a condition is met?
quiz.why: The while loop continues as long as its condition is true.

quiz.q: What does the try‑except block help you avoid?
quiz.why: It catches runtime errors so the program can continue running.

quiz.q: In the Guess the Number game, what variable should store the number of attempts?
quiz.why: The attempts variable is incremented each time the user makes a guess.

quiz.q: Which module provides the function randint() used to generate random numbers?
quiz.why: randint() is part of Python's random module.
